question: Make a time series of Euler mathoed and render 3d

slides.title: The decay problem
slides.caption: \frac{dy}{dt}=-y,\qquad y(0)=1
slides.narration: We begin with a quantity whose rate of change is the negative of its current value, starting from one at time zero.

slides.title: The exact path
slides.caption: y_{\mathrm{exact}}(t)=e^{-t}
slides.narration: The exact solution is the smooth exponential decay curve, e to the negative t.

slides.title: A ten-step grid
slides.caption: t_n=nh,\qquad h=0.1,\qquad n=0,1,\ldots,10
slides.narration: Instead of following the curve continuously, we sample time in ten equal steps of length zero point one.

slides.title: Follow the tangent
slides.caption: y_{n+1}=y_n+h\,f(t_n,y_n)=y_n+h(-y_n)
slides.narration: At each known point, Euler follows the tangent for one short time step. The slope is the differential equation evaluated at the current point.

slides.title: The update rule
slides.caption: y_{n+1}=y_n+h(-y_n)=y_n(1-h)
slides.narration: For this particular equation, adding the negative slope is the same as multiplying by one minus the step size.

slides.title: The first step
slides.caption: y_1=y_0(1-h)=1(1-0.1)=0.9
slides.narration: Starting from one, the first Euler step moves forward by zero point one and gives a new value of zero point nine.

slides.title: The numerical trajectory
slides.caption: y_0=1,\quad y_1=0.9,\quad y_2=0.81,\quad y_3=0.729,\quad \ldots,\quad y_{10}=0.3486784401
slides.narration: Repeating the same multiplication produces the Euler time series, ending at about zero point three four eight seven at time one.

slides.title: Measure the gap
slides.caption: e_n=\left|y_n-y_{\mathrm{exact}}(t_n)\right|=\left|y_n-e^{-t_n}\right|
slides.narration: At every time grid point, the error is the vertical distance between the Euler value and the exact value.

slides.title: Error accumulates
slides.caption: e_1=\left|0.9-e^{-0.1}\right|\approx0.0048374180,\qquad e_{10}=\left|0.3486784401-e^{-1}\right|\approx0.0192010011
slides.narration: After the first step the error is about zero point zero zero four eight four. By time one, it has grown to about zero point zero one nine two.

slides.title: Make error a dimension
slides.caption: P_n=\bigl(t_n,y_n,e_n\bigr)=\left(t_n,y_n,\left|y_n-e^{-t_n}\right|\right)
slides.narration: Each sample now becomes a point whose coordinates are time, numerical value, and error.

slides.title: The exact reference curve
slides.caption: C_{\mathrm{exact}}(t)=\bigl(t,e^{-t},0\bigr),\qquad 0\le t\le1
slides.narration: The exact solution lies in the zero-error plane and provides a continuous reference path for the Euler points.

slides.title: Step through time
slides.caption: P_n\longrightarrow P_{n+1},\qquad n=0,1,\ldots,9
slides.narration: Reveal the numerical trajectory one step at a time. Each point advances in time, decays in value, and rises according to its accumulated error.

slides.title: Read the 3D picture
slides.caption: \text{time}=t_n,\qquad \text{numerical value}=y_n,\qquad \text{error}=e_n
slides.narration: Time moves forward, the Euler value decays, and the third coordinate records the distance from the exact solution.

slides.title: The complete construction
slides.caption: \boxed{P_n=\left(nh,\,y_n,\,\left|y_n-e^{-nh}\right|\right),\quad y_0=1,\quad y_{n+1}=y_n(1-h),\quad h=0.1,\quad n=0,\ldots,10}
slides.narration: The construction is complete: generate the Euler values recursively, attach their absolute errors, and place the points at their corresponding times.

slides.title: FINAL ANSWER
slides.caption: \boxed{P_n=\left(nh,\,y_n,\,\left|y_n-e^{-nh}\right|\right),\quad y_0=1,\quad y_{n+1}=y_n(1-h),\quad h=0.1,\quad n=0,\ldots,10}
slides.narration: Using step size zero point one, repeatedly apply y sub n plus one equals zero point nine y sub n. Each point records time, numerical value, and absolute error from the exact exponential solution.
